programme.displayName: Amazon SQS: Basic Message Queue Test
programme.subtitle: sqs-learning-path · SAA-C03 Study Tracker update · published source revision 4
programme.description: A complete beginner Follow Along for Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) in Europe (London), eu-west-2. It updates the existing Study Tracker programme with hands-on Standard, FIFO, visibility-timeout, dead-letter queue, monitoring, and architecture exercises aligned to AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Associate (SAA-C03) message-queue decisions.
programme.learningOutcome: Use Amazon SQS safely with an approved non-root identity: create and operate Standard and FIFO queues, understand delivery and ordering behavior, configure visibility timeouts and DLQs, inspect queue health, and explain when SQS is appropriate in SAA-C03 architectures.

phases.description: Use an already approved non-root identity, select Europe (London), and verify Amazon SQS access before creating any resource.

tasks.title: 1. Verify safe non-root access to Amazon SQS in eu-west-2
tasks.feature: Preparation, regional access, and approved identity
tasks.goal: Confirm that an administrator has already authorized an existing non-root user or role for the required lab actions, then verify Amazon SQS access in Europe (London), eu-west-2.
tasks.whyItMatters: The AWS account root user has unrestricted access and is not appropriate for routine labs. This Follow Along needs an existing non-root identity that an administrator has already authorized for Amazon SQS actions such as listing, creating, configuring, sending to, receiving from, purging, and deleting the named test queues. Later optional architecture reviews can also require approved access to Lambda, SNS, S3, EventBridge, CloudWatch, EC2, Auto Scaling, or KMS. Do not create or request a custom IAM policy here. Configure AWS CLI authentication privately on the learner computer and never paste credentials, passwords, access keys, secret keys, tokens, or configuration-file contents into Study Tracker.

tasks.title: 2. Create a Standard Study Tracker worker queue and record identifiers
tasks.feature: Standard queue, queue URL, queue ARN, and producer-to-consumer architecture
tasks.goal: Create the Standard queue sqs-study-tracker-standard and record its account-specific queue URL and queue ARN.
tasks.whyItMatters: A producer sends work to an SQS queue and one or more consumers receive and process that work later. This decouples the Study Tracker producer from a potentially slow backend and buffers traffic spikes. Queue URLs identify queues in SQS API and CLI operations, while ARNs are used by features such as redrive policies and service integrations. Standard queues are appropriate when maximum throughput and at-least-once delivery are more important than strict ordering.

tasks.title: 3. Send, receive, inspect, and delete an attributed Standard message
tasks.feature: Message lifecycle, message IDs, message attributes, and explicit deletion
tasks.goal: Send one harmless Study Tracker message with a message attribute, receive it, inspect its message ID and receipt handle, and delete it after processing.
tasks.whyItMatters: SQS consumers do not remove a message merely by receiving it. A consumer receives a message, processes it, and explicitly deletes it with the current receipt handle. The returned message ID identifies the sent message; the receipt handle authorizes deletion of a specific received copy. Message attributes carry structured metadata separate from the message body.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The message operation page opens.
consoleSteps.warning: Use only the harmless sample message.

consoleSteps.title: Send an attributed message
consoleSteps.instruction: Enter Study Tracker standard message in Message body.

instructions.text: Enter Study Tracker standard message in Message body.
Add a String message attribute named StudyTopic.
Enter SAA-C03 in the attribute value.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: A send confirmation and message details are displayed.
consoleSteps.warning: Do not send personal, production, confidential, or regulated data.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The message details include its ID, body, attributes, receive count, and receipt handle information.
consoleSteps.warning: A Standard queue can return a message more than once over time.

consoleSteps.title: Delete the processed message
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The selected test message is removed.
consoleSteps.warning: Delete only the message created in this task.

tasks.title: 4. Configure retention, message size, delays, short polling, long polling, and purge behavior
tasks.feature: Standard queue delivery settings and traffic buffering
tasks.goal: Configure safe queue settings, compare short and long polling, send a delayed message, and learn when purge is appropriate.
tasks.whyItMatters: Message retention controls how long unprocessed work remains available. SQS enforces message-size limits, so large payloads should normally be placed in Amazon S3 with only an object reference in SQS. Delivery delay buffers immediate processing. Short polling can return quickly with no message; long polling waits for a message for up to 20 seconds and reduces empty receives. Purging removes all messages and must be limited to a disposable test queue.

consoleSteps.warning: Changing retention can expire existing messages after the change propagates.

tasks.title: 5. Demonstrate visibility timeout, retry behavior, and idempotent consumer design
tasks.feature: Visibility timeout, consumer crashes, duplicate processing, and in-flight messages
tasks.goal: Receive a message without deleting it, change its visibility timeout, and observe why it can become visible again for retry processing.
tasks.whyItMatters: SQS uses at-least-once delivery for Standard queues. A message can be delivered more than once, and Standard queues use best-effort ordering. If a worker crashes, loses connectivity, or does not delete a message before visibility expires, the message returns for another consumer. Consumers must therefore be idempotent: repeated processing of the same message must not create unintended repeated side effects. Set visibility timeout for expected processing time, extend it for known slow work, delete promptly after success, and use more consumers to drain traffic spikes.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The queue visibility timeout is 30 seconds.
consoleSteps.warning: Use a timeout that accommodates real processing time in production.

consoleSteps.expectedResult: The received message becomes temporarily invisible.
consoleSteps.warning: This simulates a consumer crash or an incomplete worker.

consoleSteps.title: Observe retry visibility
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The message can return and has a higher receive count.
consoleSteps.warning: Standard-queue duplication can occur even with visibility timeout, so design consumer processing to be idempotent.

tasks.title: 6. Create and test a FIFO Study Tracker queue
tasks.feature: FIFO naming, Message Group IDs, deduplication IDs, content-based deduplication, and strict ordering
tasks.goal: Create sqs-study-tracker-orders.fifo, send ordered messages in one message group, and compare FIFO behavior with Standard queues.
tasks.whyItMatters: FIFO queues require names ending in .fifo. FIFO queues preserve strict ordering within a message group and support exactly-once processing semantics through deduplication mechanisms. A MessageGroupId defines the ordered stream. A MessageDeduplicationId identifies a message for deduplication unless content-based deduplication is enabled. For SAA-C03, choose FIFO when ordered processing and duplicate suppression are requirements; choose Standard when best-effort ordering and at-least-once delivery are acceptable.

tasks.title: 7. Create a dead-letter queue and configure redrive behavior
tasks.feature: Dead-letter queues, redrive policies, maxReceiveCount, poison messages, and safe redrive
tasks.goal: Create sqs-study-tracker-dlq, configure it as the dead-letter queue for sqs-study-tracker-standard, and inspect the redrive controls.
tasks.whyItMatters: A dead-letter queue isolates failed or poison messages after a source queue receives them more than maxReceiveCount times without deletion. This prevents a repeatedly failing message from continuously consuming worker capacity. DLQs are useful for diagnosis and controlled recovery. For strict-order workloads, evaluate carefully whether a DLQ breaks the required ordering because a failed message is removed from its original sequence. Redrive should be performed slowly and only after the root cause is understood.

consoleSteps.warning: Use a higher maxReceiveCount in production when transient failures are expected.

tasks.title: 8. Review queue authorization, service access, encryption, and cross-account boundaries
tasks.feature: Queue policies, SendMessage and ReceiveMessage authorization, AWS service access, KMS, and cross-account access
tasks.goal: Inspect the test queue policy and encryption configuration without creating an IAM or queue policy.
tasks.whyItMatters: Both identity-based authorization and queue resource policies can affect SendMessage and ReceiveMessage access. Permission failures can arise from missing identity permissions, restrictive queue policies, explicit denies, cross-account requirements, or KMS permissions when a customer managed key encrypts a queue. AWS services such as SNS, S3, EventBridge, and Lambda require correctly authorized access to the target queue. For cross-account use, the queue policy and the caller identity permissions must both allow the access. This Follow Along deliberately does not invent, generate, or apply a policy.

consoleSteps.title: Open the Standard queue policy
consoleSteps.expectedResult: The current queue-policy area is visible.

tasks.title: 9. Review SQS integration architectures for SAA-C03
tasks.feature: Lambda, SNS fan-out, S3 notifications, EventBridge, EC2 workers, Auto Scaling, Amazon S3 large-message pattern, and service selection
tasks.goal: Use the test queue as the reference point for selecting SQS integration patterns and identifying their authorization boundaries.
tasks.whyItMatters: SQS supports a producer-to-queue-to-consumer design. Lambda can poll SQS in batches; failed batches and retries require idempotent handlers. SNS-to-SQS fan-out delivers a published message to multiple independent queues. S3 and EventBridge can route events to SQS when the queue policy permits the AWS service. EC2 workers can poll the queue and an Auto Scaling group can increase worker capacity based on a backlog-per-instance design. Store payloads larger than the SQS message-size limit in Amazon S3 and send a non-confidential object reference. Use SQS for durable buffered work, SNS for fan-out notifications, EventBridge for event routing, Kinesis for ordered streaming and replay use cases, and direct Lambda invocation only when durable queue buffering and independent consumer pacing are not required.

tasks.title: 10. Monitor SQS queue backlog with Amazon CloudWatch
tasks.feature: Approximate queue metrics, message-flow metrics, alarm, and queue-backlog monitoring
tasks.goal: Create a single alarm for visible Standard-queue messages, then identify the key SQS metrics used for SAA-C03 operational decisions.
tasks.whyItMatters: ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible indicates queued work waiting for consumers. ApproximateNumberOfMessagesNotVisible indicates in-flight work. ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage identifies growing delays or poison-message risk. NumberOfMessagesSent, NumberOfMessagesReceived, and NumberOfMessagesDeleted help compare producer, consumer, and deletion activity. Alarm thresholds must reflect expected processing time and capacity; a visible-backlog alarm is a simple starting point, not a complete Auto Scaling policy.

findings.message: The requested integration topics involving Lambda, SNS, S3, EventBridge, EC2, Auto Scaling, and KMS are included as safe architecture and authorization reviews. Creating these connected resources would require additional service-specific approved authorization and, for executable consumers, application code or deployment artifacts that are outside this minimal-programming SQS Follow Along.

No custom IAM or queue policy is included. Authorization troubleshooting is intentionally limited to inspection and administrator escalation because policies and cross-account access are account-specific security controls.

The protected official AWS results support SQS, SNS, EventBridge, Lambda, S3, CloudWatch, EC2 Auto Scaling, KMS, and access-control guidance. The SQS-versus-Kinesis comparison is retained as an SAA-C03 conceptual decision point but should be supplemented by the current Amazon Kinesis documentation before turning it into a separate Kinesis practical lab.

The programme identity is preserved as programme ID sqs-learning-path and display name Amazon SQS: Basic Message Queue Test. The supplied published source revision is 4; this replacement package does not publish or create a release candidate.
